name: Lane County
tax_rate: 10% county-wide (8% before Jan 1, 2023; the 2023 2-point increase was pitched for tourism facilities), plus city rates where levied and the 1.5% state tax
deadline_pattern: No open application round. Rural Tourism Marketing Program allocations are approved by the Board of Commissioners each winter (Feb 10, 2026 for 2026) and paid to ten rural cities plus the McKenzie River Chamber; event organizers apply to the receiving city, not the county
typical_open: Not applicable; allocations are formula-based on visitor data, approved in February
annual_pool: $553,172 Rural Tourism Marketing Program allocations for 2026 (10% of county TLT set aside for tourism marketing outside Eugene and Springfield); Travel Lane County received about $4.1M of TLT in FY25; FY2026-27 county TLT revenue estimated at $15.8M with about $13M in reserves
contact: Samantha Roberts, Community and Economic Development Analyst, Lane County (presented the 2026 rural tourism allocations); Lane County Administration; Samara Phelps, President and CEO, Travel Lane County
notes: Lane County does not run a competitive lodging tax grant round for outside applicants. The county passes 10% of TLT to rural cities and the McKenzie River Chamber through the Rural Tourism Marketing Program ($553,172 in 2026, Florence the largest at $237,519), contracts with Travel Lane County for destination marketing, and funds Lane Events Center ($1.92M), county parks ($877,380), the Lane County Historical Museum and covered bridge repairs from TLT. The budget committee proposed using the new HB 4148 flexibility to move lodging tax reserves into rural sheriff patrols and the courthouse (about $4.8M and $3.9M over two years), over objections from Travel Lane County; on June 23, 2026 the board voted 4 to 1 to drop the transfer and pay for one year of patrols ($1,997,919) from general fund reserves instead. Tourism Special Projects grants are referenced historically but no current round was found.

presentation.pattern: No applicant presentations; allocations are a staff-presented consent item

meeting_schedule: Board of Commissioners meets Tuesdays; rural tourism allocations taken up in February
pool_note: 2026: $553,172 distributed by formula to Coburg $33,543, Cottage Grove $52,061, Creswell $32,708, Dunes City $30,925, Florence $237,519, Junction City $24,915, Lowell $17,621, Oakridge $29,066, Veneta $17,943, Westfir $22,618 and McKenzie River Chamber $54,252. None is open to outside applicants at the county level; events must approach the receiving city or chamber. Travel Lane County's roughly $4.1M contract and the Lane Events Center and parks allocations are not competitive.

name: Salem
tax_rate: 9% city transient occupancy tax (Marion County has no county TLT), plus the 1.5% state tax
deadline_pattern: Applications open about October 10 and close mid-November for events in the following July 1 to June 30 fiscal year (Nov 18, 2024 for FY2025-26; Nov 17, 2025 for FY2026-27, with mandatory orientations Oct 7 and Oct 9, 2025 at the Salem Library). As of Nov 4, 2026 the city had not posted FY2027-28 dates on its program page, board page, news feed or FlashAlert; the pattern implies an October 2026 open and a mid-November 2026 close
typical_open: About October 10 each year, with mandatory Zoom orientation sessions in the second week of October
annual_pool: 15% of anticipated TOT revenue goes to the Cultural and Tourism Fund grants; FY2025 recommended awards totaled $791,970 against $885,670 requested (facility operating $475,170, capital $60,000, events and projects $256,800). Event grants capped at $10,000 for 501(c) nonprofits and $2,000 for non-501(c) groups
contact: Chris Neider, Program Manager III, Community Services Department, cneider@cityofsalem.net, 503-540-2361; alternate kskelly@cityofsalem.net; 555 Liberty St SE, Room 305, Salem OR 97301
notes: Salem's Grants for Promotion of Culture and Tourism are funded by the city's TOT and recommended by the nine-member Cultural and Tourism Promotion Advisory Board, with City Council making final awards through budget adoption in June. Three tracks: facility operating grants (nine established museums and venues take most of the money), capital grants up to $20,000, and event or project grants up to $10,000 for 501(c) nonprofits or $2,000 for non-501(c) groups. Events must be in city limits, open to the public, and fall in the funded fiscal year; attendance at a pre-application Zoom orientation is mandatory and applicants are limited to two event grants. The board scores applications in late winter with a passing score threshold (18.75 in 2024). No statement on HB 4148 was found. Second pass (Nov 4, 2026): no FY2027-28 cycle announcement was found on cityofsalem.net, FlashAlert or Travel Salem's industry newsletter; the last published cycle is FY2026-27 (closed Nov 17, 2025). Call 503-540-2361 to confirm whether the 2026 round opened.

name: Klamath County
tax_rate: 8% county-wide transient room tax (voters rejected an increase to 11%, Measure 18-120); Klamath Falls levies no separate city tax; plus the 1.5% state tax
deadline_pattern: Applications open at 8:00 a.m. on the first business day of March and close at 5:00 p.m. March 31 each year (March 2 to March 31, 2026; March 1 to March 31 in prior years); no late applications accepted; awards expected in early May
typical_open: March 1 or the first business day of March
annual_pool: Not published; funded from the countywide transient room tax collected by Klamath County Tax Collections
contact: Klamath County Finance Office, 541-851-2264 (2026 notice) or 541-883-4202 (earlier notices); 305 Main Street, Room 219, Klamath Falls, OR 97601; no named staff contact published
notes: Klamath County runs a long-standing annual tourism grant program funded by the countywide room tax. Applicants must attend a mandatory grant orientation in mid-March (March 12, 2026, livestreamed, no make-up sessions; one attendance per calendar year suffices) and award recipients must attend a Marketing Essentials class on May 1. A seven-member review panel appointed by the Board of County Commissioners scores applications and recommends funding levels; the board makes final decisions. The program favors events and activities that generate overnight stays in the October to May shoulder season, and also considers tourism infrastructure. Business applicants are explicitly welcome. The county also runs a separate Economic Development Grant Program whose fall 2026 cycle had an orientation on Sept 11, 2026.
